subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
title: Pillars of Swalah
overview: The pillars of swalah are the actions and words inside the prayer that it cannot do without. In this sub-strand you will learn them in order, from the niyyah and the opening takbir to the final taslim, and you will practise them with calmness and the correct sequence.

lessons.title: Niyyah, standing, the opening takbir and Al-Fatiha
objectives: Identify the first pillars of swalah.
Explain what each of these pillars means.
Show how they begin the prayer in the right order.
lessons.intro: Swalah does not begin when you unroll the mat. It begins with an intention in the heart and the words Allahu Akbar. Those first pillars decide that you have entered the prayer.
lessons.notes:
### What a pillar is
A pillar, or rukn, is an essential part inside the swalah. If it is left out on purpose, the prayer is not valid. The conditions you have already studied come before this. The pillars are what you do and say from the start of the prayer until the end. This curriculum lists: niyyah, qiyam, takbiratul ihram, reciting Al-Fatiha, rukuu, raising from rukuu, sujud, sitting between the two sujud, the final sitting, the tashahhud, the prayer for Ibrahim, taslim, tumaninah and tartib.

### The opening pillars
Niyyah is the intention in the heart. You know which prayer you are praying, such as Fajr of today. You do not have to shout the name aloud.

Qiyam means standing, for the person who is able to stand. A sick person who cannot stand prays sitting, and the standing is not forced on them.

Takbiratul ihram is the first “Allahu Akbar”, Allah is the Greatest. It closes ordinary talk and opens the prayer. Hands are raised for this takbir in the sunnah way your teacher shows. After it, you do not chat or look about on purpose.

Reciting Al-Fatiha is a pillar in every rak’ah. You already know its meaning. Recite it clearly enough that you can hear yourself when you pray alone. In a group prayer, follow the teacher’s guidance on how the follower recites.

### Order
These four come in this order: intend, stand, say the opening Allahu Akbar, then recite Al-Fatiha. Swapping them, such as reciting Al-Fatiha before the opening takbir, breaks the pillar of tartib, the correct order, which you will study again later. Learn these four names until you can pick them from a pile of cards and place them first in the line.

keyWords.meaning: a pillar; an essential part of swalah
the opening Allahu Akbar that begins the prayer

examples.problem: A boy stands on the mat, recites Al-Fatiha, and only then says Allahu Akbar. What has gone wrong?
steps: Takbiratul ihram must open the prayer.
Al-Fatiha is recited after that opening takbir.
The intention and standing come with the start, in order.
examples.answer: He recited Al-Fatiha before entering the prayer with takbiratul ihram. The opening takbir comes first, then Al-Fatiha.

activity.title: Arrange the opening pillars
materials: Flash cards: niyyah, qiyam, takbiratul ihram, reciting Al-Fatiha, and later pillars kept aside
steps: Pick the four opening pillars from the pack of cards.
Arrange them in sequence on the desk.
Explain each one in a single sentence to your group.
Write the four names and meanings in your notebook.

practice.question: What is takbiratul ihram?
practice.answer: The opening Allahu Akbar that begins the swalah.

practice.question: Where is the niyyah made?
practice.answer: In the heart. The person knows which prayer is being offered.

practice.question: In which part of the prayer is Al-Fatiha a pillar?
practice.answer: In every rak’ah, after the prayer has been opened with the takbir.

practice.question: Who may pray sitting instead of standing?
practice.answer: A person who is not able to stand, such as a sick person.

summary: Niyyah, qiyam, takbiratul ihram and Al-Fatiha are the opening pillars.
Allahu Akbar enters you into the prayer.
Al-Fatiha is recited in every rak’ah after that opening.

lessons.title: Rukuu, rising, sujud and the sitting between them
objectives: Name the posture pillars in the middle of a rak’ah.
Describe the correct shape of rukuu and sujud.
Apply tumaninah by pausing calmly in each posture.
lessons.intro: After Al-Fatiha and any short surah you add, the body moves through bowing and prostration. Rushing those postures until they look like a nod is not the prayer the Prophet (S.A.W.) taught.
lessons.notes:
### Rukuu
Rukuu is bowing. The back is kept level enough that the hands can rest on the knees, and the person stays still for a moment. While bowing, the sunnah words are “Subhana Rabbiyal Adhim”, Glory be to my Lord, the Magnificent. The pillar is the bow itself, done with calmness. The words are the Prophet’s remembrance in that bow.

### Rising from rukuu
You then stand up straight until the body is still. This rising is itself a pillar. As you rise you say “Sami’a Allahu liman hamidah”, Allah hears the one who praises Him, and when you are upright you say “Rabbana wa lakal hamd”, Our Lord, to You belongs praise.

### Sujud
Sujud is prostration. In a valid sujud, the forehead, the nose, both palms, both knees and the toes of both feet are on the ground, and you stay still. The sunnah words are “Subhana Rabbiyal A’la”, Glory be to my Lord, the Most High. Each rak’ah has two sujud.

### Sitting between the two sujud
Between the two prostrations you sit upright and remain still. A short dua taught for this sitting is “Rabbi ghfir li”, My Lord, forgive me.

### Tumaninah
Tumaninah means calmness: each pillar posture settles, even for a brief moment, instead of being pecked like a bird. The Prophet (S.A.W.) told a man who rushed his prayer to go back and pray, because he had not really prayed, and he taught him to be still in each position. Apply this today. If your rukuu has no pause, repeat the learning until the pause is there.

keyWords.meaning: bowing in swalah, with the hands on the knees
prostration, with the forehead on the ground
calmness; remaining still for a moment in each posture

examples.problem: A learner touches the forehead to the mat and lifts it at once, twice, without sitting. Which pillars are missing or incomplete?
steps: Sujud needs a moment of stillness, not a tap.
Sitting between the two sujud is a separate pillar.
Tumaninah applies to each of them.
examples.answer: The sitting between the two sujud is missing, and the sujud lacks tumaninah.

activity.title: Practise the postures in order
materials: Flash cards of rukuu, rising, sujud, sitting between sujud
steps: Arrange the four cards after the card for Al-Fatiha.
With the teacher, demonstrate rukuu, a still standing, two sujud and the sitting between them.
A partner watches whether the back settles in rukuu and whether you sit between the sujud.
Write the sunnah phrase for rukuu and the sunnah phrase for sujud in your notebook.

practice.question: What words of remembrance are said in rukuu, and what words are said in sujud?
practice.answer: In rukuu: Subhana Rabbiyal Adhim. In sujud: Subhana Rabbiyal A’la.

practice.question: Which parts of the body are placed on the ground in sujud?
practice.answer: The forehead, the nose, both palms, both knees and the toes of both feet.

practice.question: What is tumaninah?
practice.answer: Remaining calm and still for a moment in each posture of the prayer.

summary: Rukuu, rising from rukuu, two sujud and the sitting between them are pillars.
Each posture includes a moment of stillness.
The remembrance in the bow and the prostration praises Allah.

lessons.title: Tashahhud, the prayer for Ibrahim and the taslim
objectives: Identify the pillars that end the swalah.
Give the meaning of the tashahhud and the prayer for Ibrahim.
Perform the taslim to the right and to the left.
lessons.intro: The prayer does not fade out in silence. It ends with a sitting in which you greet Allah, send peace on the Prophet, pray for Ibrahim, and then give salam to those on your right and your left.
lessons.notes:
### The final sitting and the tashahhud
Sitting for the last tashahhud is a pillar. In a prayer of two rak’ahs, such as Fajr, this sitting comes after the second rak’ah. In Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha, the last sitting is the one before the salam, not the middle sitting.

The tashahhud you learn is:

“At-tahiyyatu lillahi was-salawatu wat-tayyibat. As-salamu alayka ayyuhan-nabiyyu wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh. As-salamu alayna wa ala ibadillahis-salihin. Ash-hadu alla ilaha illallah, wa ash-hadu anna Muhammadan abduhu wa rasuluh.”

Its meaning is: All greetings, prayers and good words belong to Allah. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and messenger.

### The prayer for Ibrahim
After the tashahhud in the final sitting, send prayers on the Prophet (S.A.W.) in the prayer for Ibrahim. In meaning you ask Allah to send prayers and blessings upon Muhammad and his family, as He sent prayers and blessings upon Ibrahim and his family. You say that Allah is Praiseworthy, Glorious. Your teacher will help you memorise the Arabic in steps. The pillar is to make this prayer in the final sitting.

### Taslim
Taslim ends the swalah. Turn the head to the right and say “As-salamu alaykum wa rahmatullah”, then to the left and say the same. You have now left the prayer. Tartib, the correct order, means none of these ending pillars is placed before the postures of the rak’ah.

Practise the meaning even while the long Arabic is still new, so that the tongue is not moving without the heart.

keyWords.meaning: the sitting recitation that includes the testimony of faith
the salawat asking Allah to bless Muhammad as He blessed Ibrahim
the salam to the right and left that ends the prayer

examples.problem: After two rak’ahs of Fajr, a learner gives salam at once and leaves out both the tashahhud and the prayer for Ibrahim. What pillars are missing?
steps: The final sitting should contain the tashahhud.
The prayer for Ibrahim comes before the taslim.
The taslim is correct only when it closes those pillars.
examples.answer: The tashahhud and the prayer for Ibrahim are missing. They belong in the final sitting before the taslim.

activity.title: Order the ending pillars on cards
materials: Flash cards for the final sitting, tashahhud, prayer for Ibrahim and taslim
steps: Pick these cards from the pack and place them after the sujud cards.
Discuss the meaning of the tashahhud in the group and write it in simple English.
Demonstrate the taslim to the right and then to the left.
Copy the order into your notebook.

practice.question: What does the testimony inside the tashahhud say about Allah and Muhammad (S.A.W.)?
practice.answer: There is no god but Allah, and Muhammad is His servant and messenger.

practice.question: Where in the prayer is the prayer for Ibrahim recited?
practice.answer: In the final sitting, after the tashahhud and before the taslim.

practice.question: How is the taslim performed?
practice.answer: Say As-salamu alaykum wa rahmatullah to the right, then to the left.

summary: The final sitting, tashahhud, prayer for Ibrahim and taslim end the swalah.
The tashahhud contains the testimony of faith.
Salam to the right and then the left closes the prayer.

lessons.title: The full order: tartib, calmness and daily prayer
objectives: Arrange all the pillars in the order of a two-rak’ah prayer.
Explain why following this order is following the sunnah of the Prophet (S.A.W.).
lessons.intro: Tartib means the pillars stand in their proper sequence, and tumaninah means none of them is rushed away. A two-rak’ah prayer such as Fajr is the best place to see the whole chain at once.
lessons.notes:
### Tartib in two rak’ahs
Pray a two-rak’ah swalah in this order:

1. Niyyah in the heart
2. Qiyam, standing and facing the Qibla
3. Takbiratul ihram: Allahu Akbar
4. Recite Al-Fatiha, then a short surah if you know one
5. Rukuu, with a pause
6. Rise and stand still
7. First sujud, with a pause
8. Sit between the two sujud
9. Second sujud, with a pause
10. Stand for the second rak’ah and repeat Al-Fatiha through the second sujud
11. Sit for the last tashahhud
12. Recite the tashahhud
13. Recite the prayer for Ibrahim
14. Taslim to the right and to the left

Tumaninah is not a fifteenth action parked at the end. It lives inside every bow, rise, prostration and sitting. Tartib is the rule that step 4 does not jump ahead of step 3, and the salam does not jump ahead of the tashahhud.

### Following the Prophet (S.A.W.)
He said to pray as you saw him pray. Using the pillars in order, without dropping the pause, is how a learner emulates that sunnah. Appreciate the pillars by guarding them in the five daily prayers, not only in a class demonstration. If you forget where you reached, follow the teacher’s later guidance on the prostrations of forgetfulness. Do not invent extra pillars, and do not skip Al-Fatiha because you are late. A calm, complete prayer is better than a fast, broken one.

Watch a correct demonstration, then copy it. Your own body should be able to move through the list without the card in your hand.

keyWords.meaning: performing the pillars in the correct order
one unit of swalah, from the standing through the second sujud

examples.problem: Put these mixed pillars in tartib for the start of a rak’ah: sujud, Al-Fatiha, rukuu, takbiratul ihram.
steps: The opening takbir comes before recitation.
Al-Fatiha comes before the bow.
Rukuu comes before sujud.

activity.title: Role-play a complete two-rak’ah prayer
materials: A video of the pillars if the teacher plays one
steps: Watch the video or the teacher’s demonstration of the pillars in order.
Arrange every pillar card in tartib on the floor.
In pairs or small groups, role-play a quiet two-rak’ah prayer with tumaninah. Boys and girls follow the teacher’s arrangement.
Discuss one pillar you still need to memorise, and write the full order in your notebook.

practice.question: What does tartib mean in swalah?
practice.answer: Performing the pillars in the correct order.

practice.question: Where does tumaninah belong?
practice.answer: Inside every posture, not only at the end of the prayer.

practice.question: List the ending sequence after the second sujud of the last rak’ah.
practice.answer: Sit for the tashahhud, recite the tashahhud, recite the prayer for Ibrahim, then make taslim to the right and the left.

practice.question: How does a learner appreciate the pillars?
practice.answer: By observing them in the daily prayers, calmly and in order, following the sunnah of the Prophet (S.A.W.).

summary: A two-rak’ah prayer shows the full tartib from niyyah to taslim.
Tumaninah is a pause inside each posture.
Praying in this way follows how the Prophet (S.A.W.) taught the prayer.

quiz.question: Takbiratul ihram is…
quiz.explanation: It is the pillar that enters the worshipper into swalah.

quiz.question: Al-Fatiha in swalah is…
quiz.explanation: Reciting Al-Fatiha is one of the pillars listed for swalah.

quiz.question: The correct order at the start is…
options: Niyyah and standing, opening takbir, then Al-Fatiha
quiz.explanation: Tartib places the opening takbir before Al-Fatiha.

quiz.question: Tumaninah means…
options: Being still for a moment in each posture
quiz.explanation: Calmness is a pillar that belongs inside the postures.

quiz.question: In sujud, which of these must reach the ground?
options: Only the forehead, while the feet stay up
Forehead, nose, both palms, both knees and the toes
quiz.explanation: A complete sujud uses these points of contact and includes a pause.

quiz.question: The remembrance in rukuu is…
quiz.explanation: In sujud the remembrance is Subhana Rabbiyal A’la.

quiz.question: The prayer for Ibrahim is recited…
options: In the final sitting after the tashahhud
quiz.explanation: It is a pillar of the final part of the prayer, before taslim.

quiz.question: Taslim is performed by…
options: Saying Allahu Akbar three times while jogging
Giving salam to the right and then to the left
quiz.explanation: As-salamu alaykum wa rahmatullah ends the prayer.

quiz.question: Sitting between the two sujud is…
quiz.explanation: The curriculum list includes sitting between the sujud.

quiz.question: Following the pillars calmly and in order is a way of…
quiz.answer: Emulating the sunnah of the Prophet (S.A.W.), who taught the Muslims to pray as he prayed.
quiz.explanation: Appreciating the pillars means guarding them in the daily prayers.

quiz.question: Which sequence respects tartib?
options: Sujud, rukuu, then the opening takbir
quiz.explanation: Recitation, bowing, prostration, the final words and the salam follow one another in that direction.

sources: KICD Grade 4 Islamic Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 4.0 Devotional Acts, Sub-strand 4.3 Pillars of Swalah

Pillars named in the design: niyyah, qiyam, takbiratul ihram, reciting al-Fatiha, rukuu, raising from rukuu, sujud, sitting between the sujud, the final sitting, tashahhud, the prayer for Ibrahim, taslim, tumaninah and tartib
The Prophet’s teaching to pray as he prayed, including calmness in each posture
